judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble leaves the execution date blank ("June __, 2004"), a mechanical gap that could matter for when obligations began. Otherwise the parties are identified with precision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches Schedule A and the Section 1.1 definition of "Member"; no conflict located with Section 2.1(ii) admitting LSB and DMSA on execution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital defines "Maine Act" as the "Maine Lunited Liability Company" with the word "Act" plainly dropped, a mechanical error in the very phrase creating a defined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.1 separately and completely defines "Maine Act" as 31 M.R.S.A. Chapter 13, so the recital's truncated definition is superseded rather than genuinely contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration recital with no term capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in Articles I-XVII contradicts the acknowledgment of consideration.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lead-in "unless the context otherwise requires" is conventional and does not itself create a dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs the defined terms that follow, several of which (Majority/Majority Vote, Membership Interests) are used loosely, but the interpretive rule itself fits the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference definition with no ambiguous wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13.1 does define "Additional Member", so the cross-reference lands correctly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Control" is defined by the usual power-to-direct formula; "directly or indirectly" is broad but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The term feeds Sections 12.4 (Covered Person) and 12.7 (DMSA affiliates) without visible inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Self-referential definition with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 17.10's amendment mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain definition tied to a filed public document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.1(i) instead refers to "the Certificate", an undefined term, but that mismatch is a defect of 10.1 rather than of this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line definition, no construable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently throughout Articles VI, IX and XVI.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple cross-referential definition; the OCR "tn" for "in" changes nothing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.4 does establish and maintain Capital Accounts, so the reference is sound.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Fair market value of any property" imports a valuation judgment but is standard drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule A's agreed values (Section 4.1(i)) control, and the Schedule's "$00,001.00" entry for LSB is garbled — a mismatch that surfaces in Section 4.1 rather than here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate statutory-reference definition, wholly determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Code citations in Articles VIII, XI and XIII.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names the entity; the OCR misspelling of "limited" is immaterial.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2 confirms the name; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition piles up categories ending in "any employee or agent of the Company or its Affiliates", an extremely broad sweep whose outer edge (e.g. former members, indirect agents) is not obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives Sections 12.2, 12.4 and 12.5, and because a Member is a Covered Person the exculpation runs to LSB and DMSA themselves — broad, but I found no direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Circular but harmless one-line definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article VI supplies the substance; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three-limbed period definition that is arithmetically clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the allocation machinery in Article VIII and the accounting provisions in Article X.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Such Member's interest of the profits and losses" is grammatically broken ("of" for "in"), and the definition bundles votes, profit share and distribution rights into one term used loosely elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.6 speaks of "the number of LLC Votes" and "aggregate Interests ... exceeds the number to be transferred", treating Interests as countable units, which sits awkwardly with this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list sweeps in "all policies, practices and guidelines of any governmental body" — non-binding material treated as "Laws" — and the numbering repeats "(i)", a general-vs-specific and mechanical problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Laws" is used in Sections 2.2, 2.6, 6.6 and 9.3; the breadth could expand those duties, but no operative provision directly contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise statutory citation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the recital's (truncated) reference and with Section 2.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is arithmetically clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement also defines "Majority" separately and uses the two nearly interchangeably in Section 5.5(vii)-(viii) and (xi), which invites argument about which threshold applies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Majority" is defined as a share of votes but Section 5.5(vii) uses it as a body of persons ("A Majority present in person"), a category mismatch.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates and overlaps "Majority Vote", and under Schedule A DMSA alone (51 votes) is a Majority, so quorum and consent provisions may be exercised unilaterally against unanimity provisions such as Section 17.10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any Person designated by the Members as a manager" plus automatic inclusion of Directors is workable, if loose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.1 says election as Director designates the person a Manager "for purposes of the Act" (an undefined shorthand), broadly consistent with this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining "Members" as "two (2) or more of such Persons" is odd drafting: if only one member remains, provisions keyed to "the Members" arguably have no referent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.2(ii) contemplates the departure of a Member with "remaining Members" continuing, which the two-or-more formulation strains in a two-member LLC.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Votes are fixed by reference to a schedule; determinate as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule A allocates 49/51 votes matching the Percentage Interests, but Section 16.6 calls them "LLC Votes" — an undefined variant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any amounts determined by the Members to be necessary to provide a reasonable reserve" gives an open-ended discretionary deduction that can swallow the distribution right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mandates the cash receipts and disbursements method, while Section 10.2 requires the books be kept on the accrual method "for both financial and tax reporting purposes" — a real tension; and reserves are set by the Members while Section 9.2 gives distribution timing to the Board.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Circular one-liner with no construable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article VII supplies the offices; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The tail "as determined by the unanimous written consent of the Members as adjusted from time to time" is garbled — it is unclear whether the percentages, the adjustment, or both require unanimity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(iii) lets the Secretary update Schedule A unilaterally and says such revision is not an amendment, which pulls against the unanimous-consent requirement stated here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition uses "includes" (non-exhaustive) and lists "Company" — a term the Agreement defines as Dialogo, LLC — where "corporation" was plainly meant, a mechanical error inside a definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same slip recurs in Section 3.2(i)(d) ("domestic or foreign Company's"), so the error propagates, though no operative right turns on it that I could find.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining Profits/Losses purely as taxable income under §703(a) is thin but determinate; the citation is OCR-mangled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.2(iv) aims at §704(b) compliance and Section 10.2 requires GAAP accrual books, so the tax-only definition sits somewhat loosely with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: the Board appoints, duties are cross-referenced to Section 7.4.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.1 has Officers "elected by the Board" and Section 2.1(iii)/2.6 give the Secretary further duties; broadly consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference, nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 11.1 supplies the designation as promised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard regulatory definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in Articles VIII and XIII.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional headings clause, determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against reliance on captions such as Section 12.7's "LSB's Exclusivity", which is a modest interpretive consequence rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (iii) makes the Secretary responsible for updating Schedule A and declares such updates not amendments; the phrase "as necessary to accurately reflect the information therein" is circular.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This collides with the "Percentage Interest" definition (unanimous written consent) and with Section 17.10 requiring all Members to sign any amendment — economic interests could be altered off the amendment track.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite; the Board may adopt trade names.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.6 assigns the related fictitious-name filings to the Board and Secretary; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Perpetual term with a clean dissolution carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Squares with Sections 15.2 and 15.4 on dissolution and cancellation of the Articles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific agent and address; "at any time" designation right is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Here the Members may change the agent, whereas Section 2.5 gives the parallel power over the principal office to the Board — a small allocation-of-authority inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixed address with a clear Board power to relocate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 17.1(i) sends Company notices to "the address specified in Section 2.5", which the Board may change unilaterally — a minor loose end.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Transacts business" versus "may wish to conduct business" are two different triggers in the same section, but both are workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.2 and the Secretary's role under Section 7.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific purpose ("developing Spanish language newspaper(s) and media") is joined to an unlimited general catch-all ("any lawful act or activity"), the classic general-versus-specific tension, and the specific phrase itself has no clear boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.7 bars LSB from providing services "to the extent it relates to the business" while letting DMSA compete, so the scope of "the business" defined here directly controls a one-sided restriction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long "including, but not limited to" enumeration of corporate powers; boilerplate, though the general/specific pairing is present and the sub-lettering is OCR-corrupted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several enumerated powers (borrowing, contracting with Members, leasing real property) are made subject to unanimous Board approval by Section 6.8, which expressly overrides "any other provision", so they harmonise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, unanimous approval, nothing vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Merger is not among the Section 6.8 unanimous-Board items, so Member approval governs; no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is entirely dependent on Schedule A and says nothing ambiguous on its own face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule A records LSB's contribution as "$00,001.00" against a 49% interest while DMSA contributes $50,000 for 51%, an incongruity that also bears on Section 6.8(iii)'s reimbursement of DMSA's "initial capital contributions".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short, settled propositions of LLC law.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforced by Section 5.3's partition waiver; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (ii)(a) is ungrammatical ("the respective invoices of each of DMSA", "payment form such customer") and (ii)(b) uses "Membership Interests", a term the Agreement never defines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The profit-payment reference to "Membership Interests" clashes with Sections 8.1 and 9.1 (allocations and distributions in proportion to "Percentage Interests"), and the DMSA invoice carve-out sits against Section 6.8(x)'s unanimity requirement for contracts with Members.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and mechanical; the regulation citation is truncated but identifiable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Capital Accounts drive the liquidating distribution in Section 15.3(ii), which is coherent with this provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Its Interest of the distributions" is garbled, and "such terms and conditions acceptable to the Company and each Member" leaves the advance's terms undetermined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 15.3(i) treating Member-creditors as creditors and with Section 4.3(iii)'s no-lending obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The third sentence gives Members "any and all other rights or powers of the Company", a sweeping residual grant whose boundary against the Board's authority is not drawn.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.1 vests management in the Board but is expressly "Subject to Section 5.1", producing a circular allocation of authority that a court would have to untangle.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All ordinary and necessary out-of-pocket expenses incurred by the Members on behalf of the Company" is a mandatory reimbursement with a soft standard and no approval gate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8(xiv) requires unanimous Board approval for incurring "any material liability or obligation", and the Net Cash Flow definition expressly deducts these reimbursements; the interaction is workable but not airtight.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, complete waiver with no vague term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.2 (no interest in specific Company property).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One flat prohibition; the words themselves admit of only one reading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.2(ii) expressly treats "resignation ... of a Member" as a dissolution event, so the Agreement simultaneously forbids and provides consequences for resignation — a genuine internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sub-clause (i) is mangled ("may be held at such time and place, and shall be stated in the notice"), and (vii) treats "a Majority" as persons present rather than as votes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because DMSA alone holds 51 of 100 votes, quorum, Majority Vote decisions and (xi) written consent by "a Majority" let DMSA act alone, in tension with the unanimity requirements of Sections 6.8, 13.1 and 17.10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "For purposes of the Act" uses an undefined shorthand (the defined term is "Maine Act"), and "Subject to Section 5.1" subordinates Board management to an open-ended Member power.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: With DMSA electing two of three Directors under Section 5.5(ii) while Section 6.8 demands unanimous Board action, control is split in a way that Section 6.3's tie-break (referral to Members, where DMSA again holds a majority) further complicates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and mechanical notice provisions; "any other means of communication" is broad but unlikely to be fought over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 17.1's notice regime and Section 7.4's Secretary duties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision carves out "Section 6.9 of this Agreement", but there is no Section 6.9 — the unanimity list is Section 6.8, a mechanical cross-reference error at the heart of the voting rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same phantom reference recurs in Section 6.5, and the tie-vote referral to the Members lets DMSA's 51 votes decide matters that Section 6.8 says require unanimous Board approval.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard telephonic-participation clause, determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 5.5(x) for Members; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It withholds from committees the power to take actions "described in Section 6.9", a section that does not exist in this Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Section 6.8, the intended reference is obvious but the delegation of "all the powers and authority of the Board" to a one-Director committee sits uneasily with Section 6.8's unanimity requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section is numbered 6.6 while the following section is also numbered 6.6, and it runs on from Section 6.5 in the original text — a numbering/mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Board-fixed Director compensation sits against Section 6.8(x), which requires unanimous Board approval for "other contracts with Directors", and against Section 4.3(ii)'s bar on salary to Members.
